messages:
incident-bot: Pager P2 triggered — egress-peering-saturation in pdx1 (2056789012)

sara (oncall): saw the pager. I'm on it. Paging @lee @mike for net/peering triage.

lee (eng-sre): joining — initial checks: high outbound queueing on pdx-egress-peer-3, BGP session with peer-A showing repeated withdraws, bandwidth ~95% used, tail latency up -> 504/timeout reports.

mike (netops): confirmed from net side. Peer-A is dropping due to upstream policing. Looks like a sudden large flow from a small set of prefixes. Possibly customer traffic spike + bad traffic shaping.

lee (eng-sre): action plan: 1) mitigate immediate customer impact by diverting new sessions away from pdx1 via our smart-routing policy, 2) ask netops to request peer-A rate adjustments, 3) throttle suspect prefixes at edge. Doing (1) now.

sara (oncall): please post status page draft + customer note once we have wording. I'll start handoff notes for next shift.

mike (netops): starting diversion: updating routing policy to prefer sfo1/wus4 for model-inference route-table. Applying policy now.

lee (eng-sre): applied routing override (policy id: route-override-2056). Effect should be immediate for new sessions, KV-cache warmups will be slower. Watch for increased lat/err in target regions.

raj (prod-eng): monitoring rollout metrics. Current token success rate pdx1 -> 74%, after diversion new session success for pdx-origin traffic to sfo1 -> 98% (partial roll). No regressions seen on sfo1 yet.

emily (cs): drafting customer-facing message. Two versions: short status and email. Posting drafts for review.

emily (cs): STATUS PAGE DRAFT:

"We are investigating increased request errors and elevated latency affecting Redwood customers routed via the pdx1 region. Engineers have implemented a temporary traffic diversion to alternative regions while we work with our peering partner to stabilize the connection. Impact: intermittent failures and increased latency for requests originating in or routed through pdx1. We will post updates every 15 minutes."

emily (cs): CUSTOMER EMAIL DRAFT:

"Hi — We’re writing to let you know we are currently mitigating an infrastructure issue impacting requests routed through our pdx1 region. We have temporarily diverted traffic to other nearby regions to reduce errors; most requests are succeeding. Our network team is coordinating with the peering partner to fully restore normal routing. We’ll follow up with a full incident summary."

lee (eng-sre): small tweak to status: add "no data loss" and list affected services (Host inference endpoints + embeddings). Also include timeframe and next update cadence.

emily (cs): updated status page snippet: "No data loss. Affected: model inference APIs and embeddings for some customers in pdx1. Next update in 15 minutes."

alexa (ops): tagging internal comms template — here's a short internal blurb to paste into slack #customers: "We are mitigating increased errors from pdx1 by diverting traffic. If customers ask, tell them we’ve implemented a temporary regional diversion and are working with the upstream peer; ETA for stable routing TBD."

jordan (pm): any customers on Dedicated PDx clusters? Need to surface to account teams.

emily (cs): yes — two Dedicated accounts have capacity in pdx1. Reaching out to AE + CSMs now with the email template.

sara (oncall): handoff note for next oncall: diversion in place, peer-A engagement in progress (ticket #NET-8721), edge throttling applied for suspect prefixes, status page messages being posted every 15m. If we see increased error rate in sfo1/wus4, rollback policy id route-override-2056 and notify product.

lee (eng-sre): trotted a quick ACL to rate-limit the top offending prefixes (example):

```
# rate-limit example (edge)
apply-rate-limit --scope edge-pdx1 --prefix 198.51.100.0/24 --pps 2000
```

lee (eng-sre): monitoring shows offending flows reduced after ACL; p95 lat in pdx1 improved from 2.1s -> 700ms for remaining routed flows. New sessions predominantly hit sfo1/wus4.

mike (netops): peer-A acknowledges issue and says they're applying temporary shaping on their side; they asked us to keep diversion for 30m to 1h for stabilization.

raj (prod-eng): telemetry: overall platform token success back to 99.2% after diversion. We're still tracking edge errors for a small subset of long-lived connections.

emily (cs): posted status update on status.redwood.ai: "Mitigation: traffic temporarily diverted from pdx1 to sfo1/wus4. Impact reduced. Next update in 15 minutes." (link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2056789012)

alexa (ops): any legal/comms flags for broader customer email? @jordan probably for approval on enterprise messaging.

jordan (pm): approving the customer email draft. Good to send to impacted customers and AEs.

sara (oncall): shifting monitoring to alexa for next 30m and taking a quick break. Handoff: keep diversion, monitor sfo1/wus4 for CPU/GPU pressure, escalate if token latency > 1.5s or error rate > 2%.

alexa (ops): got it — watching. Will post another status in 15m and coordinate with netops for rollback window.

(30m later)

incident-bot: Update: mitigation stable, peer-A confirms resumed normal peering.

lee (eng-sre): rolling back route-override-2056 to allow gradual traffic return to pdx1. Doing canary 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 10m.

raj (prod-eng): canary looks clean at 10/25/50. No significant error spike.

emily (cs): final status page update: "Resolved — traffic to pdx1 has been restored and the peering partner applied fixes. Services are operating normally. No customer data was lost. Postmortem to follow."

alexa (ops): closing customer comms loop; checkpoints: AE notes sent, status page updated, internal incident summary in #postmortems pending a deeper RCA.

sara (oncall): closing incident from oncall perspective. Handoff to RCA — assign to netops + eng-sre. Closing TS: 2056789435. Thanks team. :tada:
